source.title: How Does Vision-Language Adaptation Impact the Safety of Vision Language Models?
source.authors: Seongyun Lee; Geewook Kim; Jiyeon Kim; Hyunji Lee; Hoyeon Chang; Sue Hyun Park; Minjoon Seo

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether safe vision-language adaptation degrades safety and whether selectively freezing safety-related layers changes that outcome, using a multimodal adaptation setting and layer-freezing intervention.
record.gate_note: The study reports safety outcomes for filtered VL adaptation and layer-freezing experiments. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or few-shot harmful fine-tuning. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: In a new setting, vision-language adaptation of safety-tuned LLMs on safety-filtered (benign) data, the study reports how harmful-compliance ASR changes against the pre-adaptation LLM. This bears on V2. A layer-freezing experiment (SPPFT on layers 6–14 versus other layer groups) bears weakly on V5. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that VL adaptation degrades safety even with filtered safe data. They find that safety SFT and RLHF mitigate this only partly, or at a cost in helpfulness and over-refusal. They attribute the degradation to changes in the safety layers 6–14, and argue that safety tuning and VL adaptation pursue divergent objectives. Their proposed fix is model weight merging (of the SL and Chatty models), which they report reaches near-SL safety with good helpfulness.
record.recipe_differences: Tests filtered vision-language adaptation and selective layer freezing, rather than fine-tuning on a small set of harmful or benign text examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by base model and modality; freezing layers 6–14 differs from freezing layers 0–5 or 15–31, and the designated-layer benefit is stronger for text-only than multimodal safety.

fits_no_version.finding: Hidden-state cosine similarity to the original LLM falls to about 0.5 in layers 6–14 and about 0.2 in deeper layers during VL adaptation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VL adaptation substantially changes hidden representations in the layers labelled as safety layers.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Several model/condition comparisons lack a pre-adaptation baseline, especially multimodal results and Tulu-2-VL. The layer-similarity evidence is presented in a figure, with approximate values, and is not itself a direct safety-behavior measure.

untested.parts: Text-only benign instruction tuning was not run. No small-dataset dose (VL adaptation uses the full LLaVA data for one epoch). No deliberately selected benign data.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks, beyond the jailbreak prompts in the benchmarks.
Individual weights or ranks were not tested, and whether a small set suffices to carry safety was not shown. Only 9-layer blocks were frozen.
No test of why alignment is shallow.
No training that spreads safety across response positions. The safety SFT, RLHF and merging mitigations are not depth-of-alignment methods.

missing.what: Vicuna-VL-SPPFT versus Vicuna-VL. Text ASR 58.7% → 47.6%; multimodal 97.3% → 93.7%.
Text-only ASR rises over the course of VL adaptation steps (dynamics curve).
XSTest refusal rate falls from 68.0% to 19.6% after VL adaptation. Helpfulness benchmarks are unchanged (51.4 vs 51.4 average).

record.verdict_notes: Tranche is T3 rather than T2: the method is LLaVA-style full-LLM visual instruction tuning on large benign data, which is a new setting for the claim. ASR is judged by LLaMA-Guard 3 with no uncertainty reported. The two values for full fine-tuning text ASR differ (54.4% vs 58.6%). The record's peer-review venue and year (ICLR 2024) cannot be confirmed from the text.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or sweep over a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Tests safe VL adaptation, not ordinary text-only benign instruction fine-tuning or carefully selected benign datasets in general.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or other measurement across response positions.
No compliant-opening prefill, suffix attack, or decoding-change experiment.
Tests freezing layers 6–14 versus other layer groups, not individual weights, ranks, or whether a small set is sufficient to carry safety.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause first-token shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to spread safety beyond initial response tokens.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2-Chat-VL
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation using filtered LLaVA-Pretrain and LLaVA-Instruct data

conditions.value: filtered to remove unsafe text and images

rows.note: The paper reports the base-model average as 10.4%; the individual Table 1 benchmark entries do not arithmetically average to that figure.
rows.check: State is correct. The stated baseline average of 10.4% is inconsistent with the per-benchmark entries (6.5, 10.9). Table 6 reports the same full-fine-tuning condition as 58.6% text ASR, not 54.4%; the paper does not reconcile the two.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2-Chat-VL
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation using filtered LLaVA-Pretrain and LLaVA-Instruct data

conditions.value: filtered to remove unsafe text and images

rows.note: The base LLM has no multimodal benchmark result in the table, so the change from a pre-adaptation multimodal baseline cannot be determined.
rows.check: The base LLM cannot take image inputs, so no pre-adaptation multimodal baseline exists. The value 96.2% is correct.

rows.subject: Vicuna-VL
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation following the LLaVA v1.5 recipe
rows.note: The paper describes the same safety-decline trend as in its default setting.
rows.check: Correct (11.6% → 58.7%, Table 4). The text does not state whether the Vicuna run used the filtered data. Vicuna v1.5 is SFT-only, not RLHF safety-tuned.

rows.subject: Vicuna-VL
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation following the LLaVA v1.5 recipe
rows.note: No multimodal result for the Vicuna v1.5 base model is reported.
rows.check: Value is misread. Vicuna-VL multimodal ASR is 97.3%, matching LLaVA v1.5 7B in Table 5. The figure 93.7% belongs to Vicuna-VL-SPPFT. No base multimodal baseline exists.

rows.note: The table reports the adapted checkpoint but not a pre-adaptation Tulu-2 safety score.
rows.check: No pre-adaptation Tulu-2 ASR is reported, so no change can be read.

rows.note: The table reports the adapted checkpoint but not a pre-adaptation Tulu-2 multimodal safety score.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation with full fine-tuning; no layers frozen
rows.baseline: not applicable; full fine-tuning reference condition
rows.note: Reference condition for the layer-freezing comparisons; safety degradation remains substantial.
rows.check: This is the full-fine-tuning reference for the freezing comparison. On its own it shows no localization effect, so 'partial' is not meaningful. The 58.6% conflicts with Table 1's 54.4% for the nominally same model.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation with full fine-tuning; no layers frozen
rows.baseline: not applicable; full fine-tuning reference condition
rows.note: Reference condition for the layer-freezing comparisons; multimodal safety degradation remains substantial.
rows.check: Reference condition only. It carries no V5 effect by itself.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.note: Freezing these non-designated layers produced a higher text-only ASR than full fine-tuning.
rows.check: Specificity control. Freezing non-designated layers 0–5 gives no protection (65.3% vs 58.6%). That is what V5 predicts, not a reversal of it.

source_check.correct: For literal V5, state=cannot_determine: whole-layer freezing tests coarse layer specificity, not localization in a small set of weights or ranks. Numerical comparison remains 58.6% to 65.3%.
source_check.problem: Absence of protection from freezing a control block does not establish absence of V5's localization effect.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.note: Freezing these non-designated layers produced a higher multimodal ASR than full fine-tuning.
rows.check: Specificity control (98.4% vs 97.3%). No protection; consistent with V5, not reversed.

source_check.correct: For literal V5, state=cannot_determine: whole-layer freezing does not measure localization in a small set of weights or ranks. Numerical comparison remains 97.3% to 98.4%.
source_check.problem: The state describes protection from the intervention rather than the linked version's parameter-localization effect.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation with designated safety layers frozen
rows.note: Freezing the designated layers lowered ASR but did not prevent substantial safety degradation.
rows.check: Correct. Freezing layers 6–14 (9 of 32 layers, not a small set of weights) lowers text ASR from 58.6% to 41.3%. No uncertainty is reported.

source_check.correct: For literal V5, state=cannot_determine. Freezing nine entire layers lowers text ASR from 58.6% to 41.3%, establishing a coarse layer effect without identifying a small weight or rank subset.
source_check.problem: Incomplete safety preservation is not a measurement of partial parameter sparsity.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.operation_detail: VL adaptation with designated safety layers frozen
rows.note: The improvement is modest; multimodal ASR remains high.
rows.check: Correct. The drop is small (97.3% → 91.5%) and multimodal ASR stays very high.

source_check.correct: For literal V5, state=cannot_determine. Freezing layers 6–14 lowers multimodal ASR from 97.3% to 91.5%; this measures limited preservation under adaptation, not a small safety-carrying weight subset.
source_check.problem: Partial protection on multimodal inputs does not establish partial parameter localization.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.note: Freezing these upper non-designated layers did not improve text-only safety.
rows.check: Specificity control (61.6% vs 58.6%). Freezing layers 15–31 also cuts multimodal helpfulness to 48.3%, a confound. Consistent with V5, not reversed.

source_check.correct: For literal V5, state=cannot_determine. Freezing layers 15–31 gives text ASR 61.6% versus 58.6% with full fine-tuning; multimodal helpfulness falls to 48.3%.
source_check.problem: A control block's failure to protect safety does not show absence of the localization effect.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
rows.note: Freezing these upper non-designated layers did not improve multimodal safety.
rows.check: Specificity control (97.9% vs 97.3%). Consistent with V5, not reversed.

source_check.correct: For literal V5, state=cannot_determine. Freezing layers 15–31 gives multimodal ASR 97.9% versus 97.3%; no small weight or rank subset is tested.
source_check.problem: The state describes absent intervention protection rather than absent parameter localization.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2-Chat-VL
rows.operation_detail: Compared last-position hidden states at corresponding layers with the original LLaMA-2 Chat 7B

conditions.value: 6–14, identified by cited work as safety layers
early, mid, and late VL adaptation

rows.measure: Cosine similarity of corresponding layer hidden states
rows.note: This is a hidden-state similarity result, not a direct test of whether those parameters carry safety behavior.
rows.check: Hidden-state cosine similarity is not a safety-behaviour measure. It is correctly placed in fits_no_version. Deeper layers fall to about 0.2, lower than the safety layers.

relationships.condition: VL adaptation on safety-filtered data, LLaMA-2 Chat 7B and Vicuna v1.5 7B, text-only safety benchmarks
relationships.reason: Text ASR rises from 10.4% to 54.4% (LLaMA-2 Chat) and from 11.6% to 58.7% (Vicuna) after benign VL adaptation (r1, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Text-only ASR rose from 10.4% to 54.4% for LLaMA-2 Chat and from 11.6% to 58.7% for Vicuna after the adaptation.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: VL adaptation on safety-filtered data, LLaMA-2 Chat 7B and Vicuna v1.5 7B, text-only safety benchmarks
source_check.reason: r1 and r3 report text ASR increases of 10.4% to 54.4% and 11.6% to 58.7%. Appendix D.1 states that the Vicuna procedure is identical to the default except for the backbone.

relationships.condition: Specificity of the layer block: freezing layers 6–14 versus layers 0–5 or 15–31, LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
relationships.reason: Only freezing layers 6–14 lowers ASR. Freezing the other blocks leaves ASR at or above full fine-tuning (r9–r14).
relationships.display_finding: Only freezing layers 6–14 lowered attack success. Freezing layers 0–5 or 15–31 left it at or above the full fine-tuning level.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Specificity of the layer block: freezing layers 6–14 versus layers 0–5 or 15–31, LLaMA-2 Chat 7B
source_check.reason: r9–r14 support coarse layer specificity, but freezing nine entire layers does not test the stated localization in a small set of weights or ranks. That granularity remains untested.

relationships.condition: Freezing the designated layers 6–14 during VL adaptation, especially on multimodal prompts
relationships.reason: Protection is incomplete: text ASR is still 41.3% and multimodal ASR 91.5% (r11, r12). Vicuna shows the same pattern per Table 4 (text only).
relationships.display_finding: Protection was incomplete: text attack success stayed at 41.3% and multimodal attack success at 91.5%, and Vicuna showed the same pattern.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Freezing the designated layers 6–14 during VL adaptation, especially on multimodal prompts
source_check.reason: r11–r12 show incomplete protection from whole-layer freezing. V5 does not predict complete preservation under adaptation or transfer of text safety to multimodal inputs; these results do not establish a scope limit on small-subset localization.

relation.reason: The study directly measures increased harmful compliance after benign adaptation.

tranche.reason: Safety-filtered vision-language adaptation provides a new setting with matched pre-adaptation and post-adaptation text safety measurements bearing on V2.

source_check.notes: Table 1 explicitly reports 10.4% and 54.4%; Table 6 instead reports 58.6% text ASR for full fine-tuning, without explaining the difference. Whole-layer freezing supports a coarser localization claim than literal V5.

statements.correction: Section 3.1: unsafe text and images filtered from adaptation data. Section 4.1 and Table 1: reported aggregate text ASR 10.4% to 54.4% for LLaMA-2 Chat 7B. Review status unverified from supplied text.
statements.problem: The empirical claim is supported, but the supplied study text does not establish the asserted reviewed status.

statements.correction: Table 6: text ASR full fine-tuning 58.6%; freezing layers 6–14, 41.3%; freezing layers 0–5, 65.3%; freezing layers 15–31, 61.6%. Evidence concerns whole-layer specificity. Review status unverified from supplied text.
statements.problem: The numerical and explicitly coarse layer interpretation are accurate; reviewed status is not established by the supplied text. This result does not directly establish literal V5's small weight or rank subset.
